provenance.paper_title: RGB-Only Reconstruction of Tabletop Scenes for Collision-Free Manipulator Control

latest_version.version_label: arXiv v2 / ICRA 2023 paper reviewed on 2026-08-31

representation_paths.memory_component: fixed NeRF-derived scene mesh and Euclidean full signed distance field used by the manipulator controller

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. III-A Neural Scene Reconstruction from RGB Images
evidence.paraphrase: Multiple RGB observations are consolidated into a per-scene NeRF; a polygonal mesh and bounding-volume hierarchy are extracted, and signed distances are queried to form an ESDF suitable for downstream robotic planning.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. III-B Manipulator Control Problem
evidence.paraphrase: After reconstruction, the scene mesh is loaded into a sampling-based model-predictive controller. The controller repeatedly queries the fixed signed-distance representation to generate collision-free robot motions toward later target poses.

adjudication_notes: Included under the guide's fixed-map rule: the RGB-derived mesh/ESDF persists beyond formation and is an operative input to subsequent manipulator-control decisions.

The paper describes fast per-scene NeRF optimization during memory formation, but does not update the reconstructed scene during the downstream MPC phase. Formation-time optimization does not raise the management tier, so the architecture is T1.
